extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for claiming the benefit of, or priority to, earlier U.S. or foreign patent applications (including provisional claims) and related file-history notation, status handling, and required statements under 37 CFR 1.78 and 1.55.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of preprinted prior application data
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is an error in the preprinted prior application data, correction or entry of the data in the Patent Data Portal database can be made by technical support staff of the Technology Center, if appropriate. If the error was an applicant error, the examiner should require correction via a corrected or supplemental application data sheet or an amendment, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon entry of corrected data, print a new bib-data sheet and scan into the file. A petition for an unintentionally delayed benefit claim may also be required. See MPEP § 601.05 et seq., § 211.02(a), and § 211.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of prior application information is not conclusive of entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclusion of prior application information in the patent does not necessarily indicate that the claims are entitled to the benefit of the earlier filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and practitioners must check entitlement separately. See MPEP § 2136.03, § 2154.01(b), and § 306 for assignment of information and entitlement analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bib-data sheet foreign priority listing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A bib-data sheet must include the application number, country (or intellectual property authority), day, month, and year of each foreign application to which priority is claimed; the examiner should check this information for accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a foreign application listed on the oath/declaration or ADS is not on the bib-data sheet and the claim is proper, provide information to the Legal Instrument Examiner for correction. If applications are from countries not qualifying for benefits under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d), request removal of references. If there is an error on the oath/declaration or ADS, require a new oath/declaration or ADS and consider a petition for unintentionally delayed priority (see MPEP § 214.02). If foreign priority is claimed, the bib-data sheet must acknowledge it and the Office action and bib-data sheet must indicate whether the conditions of 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) have been met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple foreign priority claims must be listed individually
rubrics_metrics.description: If the filing dates of several foreign applications are claimed, information regarding each foreign application is to be entered on the bib-data sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each foreign application must be individually identified (number, country, filing date) and checked for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application status designations and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard status categories: 'new' (nonprovisional not yet acted on by examiner), 'rejected' (contains an unanswered examiner's action prior to allowance), 'amended' (applicant has replied to an examiner action), 'allowed/in issue' (examined and determined to meet statutory requirements; notice of allowance sent), 'abandoned' (removed from pending docket for various reasons), 'incomplete' (not entitled to a filing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment filed prior to the first Office action does not alter 'new' status. RCE is not a type of new application filing. Abandonment examples include failure to take appropriate action, failure to pay issue fee, or lapse of provisional after 12 months. See MPEP §§ 203.01–203.06 and § 706.07(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status inquiries: Patent Center and timing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Status information is available through Patent Center (public and private views). Private view requires Customer Number association. Applicants and other persons should check Patent Center for status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Application Assistance Unit (AAU) can assist if needed. For allowed applications, Form PTOL-37 and PTOL-85 timelines: inquire if PTOL-85 not received within three months of PTOL-37. Amended applications are expected to be acted on within two months after examiner receives the amendment; do not inquire until 5–6 months after applicant reply unless six months have elapsed with no response to avoid abandonment. See MPEP § 203.08.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of receipt as prima facie evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A stamped postcard or Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt for papers filed is prima facie proof of receipt of such papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where such proof indicates timely filing, submission of a copy of the receipt with a copy of the reply ordinarily obviates need for a petition to revive. Proof of receipt of a timely reply to a final action will obviate the need for a petition to revive only if the reply was in compliance with 37 CFR 1.113. See MPEP § 503 and USPTO guidance on e-office-action program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Congressional and other official inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence and inquiries from the White House, Members of Congress, embassies, and heads of Executive departments/agencies are to be cleared and transmitted to the appropriate USPTO offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmit such inquiries immediately to the Office of Policy and International Affairs and/or Office of Governmental Affairs and notify staff by phone (provided phone numbers). This ensures uniform handling and compliance with Department of Commerce directives. See MPEP § 203.08(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.78: specific reference requirement for benefit under earlier national applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For a later-filed application to be entitled to the benefit of an earlier national application under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c), the later-filed application must contain a specific reference to the earlier-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, the specific reference must be in the application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76). For applications filed prior to that date, the reference may be in the ADS or in the first sentence(s) of the specification. See MPEP § 210 and 37 CFR 1.78 summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.78(a) provisional benefit claim requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) of a prior-filed provisional application: later-filed nonprovisional/international apps must be filed not later than 12 months after the provisional (subject to paragraph (b)); each prior provisional must name the inventor(s), be entitled to a filing date, and have the basic filing fee paid within the required period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The later-filed application must contain or be amended to contain a reference identifying each prior provisional by provisional application number; for nonprovisionals the reference must be in an ADS (§ 1.76(b)(5)). The reference must be submitted during the pendency of the later-filed application and within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the later-filed application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior-filed provisional. Failure to timely submit the reference is considered a waiver of benefit except as provided in § 1.78(c) and certain pre-November 29, 2000 exceptions. See 37 CFR 1.78(a)(1)–(5) and MPEP § 211.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.55: claiming priority to an earlier foreign application
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim for priority to an earlier foreign application must identify the foreign application; for applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, the claim must be presented in the application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.55 contains provisions on: which foreign priorities may be claimed (a); time for filing nonprovisional claiming priority (b); restoration of right of priority (c); time for filing a priority claim in 111(a) and 371 national stage apps (d); delayed claims (e); timing for filing certified copy (f); filing of certified copy and translations (g); when a certified copy requirement is satisfied by a copy in another U.S. patent/application (h); priority document exchange (i); interim copy filing (j); special requirements for apps filed on/after March 16, 2013 (k); inventor's certificates (l); timing for international design apps (m); presentation in oath/declaration for pre-Sept 16, 2012 apps (n); applicability for 386(a)/(b) (o); and non-extendable time periods subject to limited exceptions (p). See MPEP § 210 and 37 CFR 1.55 summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.55/1.78 statement requirement for first-inventor-to-file transition applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition applications (nonprovisional filed on/after March 16, 2013 that claim priority to or benefit of an application filed before March 16, 2013) must include a statement if the later-filed transition application contains, or contained at any time, a claim to a claimed invention with an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must be provided within the later of: four months from the actual filing date of the later-filed application, four months from entry into the national stage (37 CFR 1.491), sixteen months from the filing date of the prior-filed application, or the date a first claim with an effective filing date on/after March 16, 2013 is presented in the later-filed application. Exceptions: nonprovisional international design applications; if the nonprovisional discloses only subject matter also disclosed in a priority or benefit application filed prior to March 16, 2013; or if the nonprovisional claims only priority to/benefit of an application filed on/after March 16, 2013. Applicant need only state that such a claim exists and is not required to identify which claims or how many. The Office may issue a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 if contradictory positions are taken. See MPEP § 210–211 and 37 CFR 1.55(k), 1.78(a)(6)/(d)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) checkbox and filing receipt reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: The ADS (Form PTO/AIA/14) and the transmittal letter for 35 U.S.C. 371 national stage filing (Form PTO-1390) include a checkbox to make the 37 CFR 1.55/1.78 statement; presence or absence of the statement is reflected on the filing receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should carefully and promptly review filing receipts and may request a corrected filing receipt if information is incorrect to ensure examination under the correct statutory framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirements for benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 119(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 119(e), an application may have the same effect as the earlier application as to an invention disclosed in the manner provided by 35 U.S.C. 112(a) if filed before patenting/abandonment and if it contains or is amended to contain a specific reference to the earlier filed application; failure to submit such an amendment within the required pendency time may be considered waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may establish procedures, including fee (41(a)(7)), to accept an unintentionally delayed submission of an amendment. For provisional claims under 119(e)(1), the later-filed nonprovisional must be filed not later than 12 months after the provisional; the Director may extend by up to 2 months for unintentional delay under regulations. See statutory text quoted (35 U.S.C. 120, 35 U.S.C. 119(e)) and MPEP § 211.
